```{r include=FALSE,echo=FALSE}
source(file="fisherXY.R")
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)

GSS <-read.dta(file="GSS2016.dta")
GSS <- droplevels(GSS)
mydata <- select(GSS,race,cappun)
mydata <- na.omit(mydata)

```

# Introduction

<!--In this section you explain what you are trying to show.  Where did the data come from?  What is the research or other question you are trying to answer?.  If you skimp in this section expect to be marked down in your grade. Paint a picture of the project a couple of paragraphs is expected!-->

Is attitude toward capitol punishment (cappun) independent of race (race)?
If not, then whose view differs from whom??

Based of the dataset GSS, is the attitude toward capitol punishment independent from the race of the individual? 

$H_0$: There is no relationship between the attitude of an individual towards capitol punishment and their race. 

$H_A$: There is a relationship between the attitude of an individual towards capitol punishment and their race.

## Descriptive Results

### Graphical Descriptive Results

<!--Graphical results here.  Make sure to show your code.  Provide appropriate labels for axes, giving units if possible, and provide a good title for the graph, too.  Use the graphical results to describe the patterns if any that exist in the data as focused toward the research question. Bottom line is to explain the features of the graph that are relevant to conforming or departing to what is expected by your null hypothesis !-->

```{r}
barchartGC(~cappun + race,data=GSS)
barchartGC(~cappun + race,data=GSS, type="percent")

```

According to this bar chart, there was a higher percentage of white individuals that favored capitol punishment over those who opposed it. The bar chart also shows that a higher percentage of black individuals opposed capitol punishment over those who favored it. As for the other category, the percentage of those who opposed and favored capitol punishment were closer in percentages.

## Now with The Most data (fewer variables gives more data points)

### Numerical Descriptive Results

<!--Numerical results go here. Use the numerical results to describe the patterns if any that exist in the data as focused toward the research question!-->

```{r}
table1 <- xtabs(~cappun + race, data=GSS)
rowPerc(table1)
colPerc(table1)
```


According to this table, there appears to be a higher percentage of white individuals that favor capitol punishment than those who oppose it. There also appears to be a lower percentage of black and other individuals that favor capitol punishment than those who oppose it. 65.1% of white individuals favored capitol punishment and 34.9% of white individuals opposed it. 42.63% of black individuals favored capitol punishment and 57.37%  of black individuals opposed it. 55.2% of other individuals favored capitol punishment and 44.8% of other individuals opposed it. 

## Now with More data

## Inferential Results

<!--State hypothesis clearly.  Make sure your discussion of the inferential test covers all the aspects that the test output produces, such as test statistic, p-value etc.  Make a decision about the null hypothesis, explain the assumptions on which the selected test/procedure was based, and why the chosen procedure satisfys the assumptions and is appropriate to answer the research question!-->

```{r}
chisq.test(table1)
chisqtestGC(table1)
fisher.test(table1)
```

The p-value is 0.00000000000000022 which is less than 0.05. This means we will reject the null hypothesis and that we conclude that there is a relationship between an individuals attitude towards capitol punishment and the race of the individual.

## More data version

```{r}
fisherXY(GSS$cappun,GSS$race,confL=0.05) 
```

The fisherXY test displays that all races have a difference in their attitude towards capitol punishment as each of the races displayed have a p-value that is less than 0.05. The p-value of white and black is 0.00000000000000022. The p-value of white and other is 0.002607. The p-value of black and other is 0.001564. As is shown, the p-values are less than 0.05 and therefore we can reject the null hypothesis. Each also have different odd ratios. 

# Discussion and Conclusion

<!--Discussion and conclusion here.  If you found a relationship be sure to consider whether the relationship occurs because one of the variavbles causes the other, or whether they perhasps are related for some other reason.  Watch the chapter 6 videos from the GeorgeTown videos collection.!-->
Is the attitude of an individual toward capitol punishment independent from their race? 

Based off of the information gathered from tests and plots performed, we reject the null hypothesis as the p-value resulted in the values below 0.05. The fisherXY test showed that each race is different regarding their attitude towards capitol punishment. The results p-values of the different races included 0.002607, 0.001564, and 0.00000000000000022. Thiis is why we can reject the null hypothesis. We can conclude that there is a relationship between the attitude of an individual towards capitol punishment and race. The data displayed that there were higher percentages of white individuals favoring capitol punishment, higher percentages of black individuals opposing capitol punishment, and a close percentage of other race individuals regarding favoring or opposing capitol punishment.
